label: AI-judged (GLM-5.3, blind) on SIMULATED learners; not real-learner proof

recs.subject: spanish
dislikes: rewrites of the same idea three times
errors: V1, Block 2: 'Only vamos looks like a regular -ir verb' is false — vamos ends in -amos, the regular -ar ending (cf. hablamos); no form of ir resembles a regular -ir form (cf. vivimos), and vas/va/vais/van equally resemble -ar endings.

V2, Block 3: the table titled 'The six forms of ir' displays only four persons (yo and nosotros rows missing) and, as rendered, no Spanish forms; the c1 hint 'you (informal) is the second row' does not match the table as shown.
recs.objective_note: Both teach the same objective: conjugating irregular ir and using a/al to state destinations (Voy al trabajo). V1 explicitly covers the adondo component (Adonde? in Blocks 4 and 7 and check c4); V2 only glosses 'to where?' and never shows the Spanish word adonde, so that sub-objective is thinly covered but not replaced.
